what_happened.line: Assessors signed the FY2026 preliminary real estate and personal property tax warrants after reconciling mismatched parcel counts between the town's Munis system and the state LA4 filing.
The board voted to release the parcel at 222 West Townsend Road from chapter-land status, clearing it for potential sale.
The board also signed two motor vehicle excise commitment warrants covering separate batches of bills.
Staffing shortages are limiting field inspections; the office is weighing carrying mace on site visits, using the police boat for lakefront parcels, and adding a seasonal employee.
The board opted to move forward with an in-house design for the senior means-tested tax exemption brochure to meet a September 3rd deadline.

why_it_matters: Signing the preliminary tax warrant sets the real estate, personal property, and motor vehicle excise bills that get mailed to residents this cycle.
A parcel leaving chapter-land status changes what that property owner can do with the land and how it's taxed going forward.
The senior means-tested exemption brochure and application, due by September 3rd, affects which seniors can apply for reduced tax bills this year.
watch_next: Senior means-tested exemption application deadline, September 3rd
Possible special board meeting before mid-July on the pending 41A exemption appeal

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the meeting's one recorded vote and on most dollar-and-count figures tied to motor vehicle excise, but they diverge sharply elsewhere: many figures our minutes captured (the FY2026 tax warrant total, parcel-count reconciliation, circuit-breaker/means-tested exemption numbers, Chapter 61 parcel counts) have no corresponding figure in the official minutes at all, and two decisions — the senior-exemption brochure and the DOR-directives status item — are described in ways that actually conflict rather than merely differ in detail. Attendee names are also badly mis-transcribed and the chair/vice-chair roles are swapped, which a reader should verify against the roster rather than trust either record's role labels alone.
